source_span: this is not impacting Nvidia and Broadcom in 2027... but we believe this could affect downstream components, like memory, optical, and other components like power management and analog parts in a bear case
source_chain: US data center power scarcity (57GW gross / 32GW net through 2028) concentrates energization among large, credit-worthy hyperscalers/neoclouds (60-95% of coming capacity) THEREFORE Nvidia and Broadcom stay safe for their combined $800bn 12-month AI revenue outlooks, with Nvidia preferred for its broadest geographic/customer footprint THEREFORE any disruption from the shortfall lands downstream, on memory, optics and small-dollar power/analog components, and ASICs risk losing share to GPUs; invalidation: a slowdown signal (chip capacity that can't be deployed, causing customers to push out or cancel orders) is what would actually spread that disruption through the chain.
pulse_chain: Power scarcity (57GW gross / 32GW net, 32-42GW / 34-43% short through 2028) concentrates capacity access among large, credit-worthy hyperscalers/AI-cloud players (60-95% of capacity) THEREFORE Nvidia/Broadcom (~90% of accelerator-chip share) stay convicted-safe for their combined $800bn outlooks, Nvidia named preference on its footprint THEREFORE the disruption, if power bites, lands on memory, optics and small-dollar components, with ASICs at risk to GPUs; carried invalidation is whether TSM's Oct 15 guidance confirms or walks back Goldman's $85bn/$98bn 2027/2028 capex model, deciding power-constrained vs. equipment-supply as the binding limit.
why: The pulse reproduces Morgan Stanley's scarcity-to-concentration-to-chip-safety-to-downstream-exposure chain in the same order and direction with correct attribution, and layers on Goldman's memory counter-read and the TSM print as an added falsifiable test rather than reversing or misattributing Morgan Stanley's own argument.
